meta.title: Inversion
meta.subtitle: Clear the air on climate misinformation
meta.author: Jordan Heaton
meta.course: PWS 180: Climate Change: Science and Solutions (BYU)
meta.intro: Each post is legit or uses a classic misinformation trick. Name the trick to clear the air.
meta.privacy: No login. Your answers aren’t saved or sent anywhere (the site’s host does count page visits).
meta.takeaway: Reply warm, plus one fact: start with something you agree on, give the fact, name the trick, and keep it kind.

techniques.name: Fake Experts
techniques.hint: Wrong-field credentials, or a crowd of names posing as experts
techniques.definition: Presenting someone as an authority when their expertise isn't in climate science, or making a tiny minority look like a real scientific debate.
techniques.notThis: Fake Experts needs someone’s credentials, or a crowd of names, standing in for evidence.

techniques.name: Logical Fallacy
techniques.hint: Broken logic: one cause for everything, a false choice
techniques.definition: Reasoning that breaks in a way the other four tricks don't name: one cause for everything, a false choice, attacking the messenger, "someone else is worse," or "it happened naturally before, so it's natural now." Every trick is bad reasoning; this is the category for the rest.
techniques.notThis: Logical Fallacy needs reasoning that breaks in a way none of the other four tricks names.

techniques.name: Impossible Expectations
techniques.definition: Demanding a certainty from the science that it can't give, like an exact date or a perfect forecast, before accepting it or acting on it. (Demanding perfection from people is a false choice, under Logical Fallacy.)
techniques.notThis: Impossible Expectations needs a demand for certainty the science can’t give.

techniques.name: Cherry Picking
techniques.hint: Spotlights the data that fits, hides the rest
techniques.definition: Choosing the one year, place, or data point that supports a claim while ignoring the larger body of evidence.
techniques.notThis: Cherry Picking needs one moment or data point standing in for the trend.

techniques.name: Conspiracy Theory
techniques.hint: Assumes a secret plot behind the science
techniques.definition: Claiming that scientists, agencies, or "they" are secretly coordinating a lie, and treating any counter-evidence as part of the cover-up.
techniques.notThis: Conspiracy Theory needs a secret plot or a hidden “they.”

techniques.name: Looks Legit
techniques.definition: Not every post is misinformation. Accurate posts make claims that match the evidence and don't stretch it. A named source helps, but real sources get stretched too, and a true post may not cite one.
techniques.notThis: Looks Legit needs a claim that matches the evidence. A real source alone isn’t enough.

posts.text: finally someone with real credentials says it 👇 tag someone who needs to hear this

graphic.quote: CO₂ is too small a slice of the air to warm anything.

posts.explanation: DDS means dentist. Fixing teeth isn’t climate expertise, and neither is a blue check. Ask what the expert studies.
posts.fact: CO₂ is about 0.04% of the air but up over 50% since before industry. Small shares matter: 0.05% blood alcohol is a Utah DUI.

sources.label: Broken record: Atmospheric carbon dioxide levels jump again
sources.check: Checked 2026-11-04. CO₂ "averaged 424.0 parts per million (ppm) in May" (424 ppm = 0.042% of the air); "Carbon dioxide levels are now more than 50% higher than they were before the onset of the industrial era."

sources.label: 0.05 BAC Law
sources.check: Checked 2026-11-04. "Utah became the first state in the nation to lower its legal per se Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) limit for driving from 0.08 to 0.05"; in effect since December 30, 2018.

sources.label: The Causes of Climate Change
sources.check: Checked 2026-10-31. "About 90% of this heat is then absorbed by greenhouse gases and re-radiated, slowing heat loss to space."

alsoFair.note: “Too small to matter” is a fallacy too. But the post is selling the speaker: a dentist dressed up as the expert.

whyNot.legit: A blue check and a “Dr.” aren’t evidence. DDS means the speaker studies teeth, not the atmosphere.
whyNot.conspiracy: Nothing here claims a secret plot. The pitch is the speaker’s title.

posts.text: Utah Division of Water Resources: 2023 was the BIGGEST snowpack Utah has EVER recorded ❄️ remember when they said climate change was killing our winters?? lol

image.alt: Deep snow on the slopes and cabins of Little Cottonwood Canyon near Alta, with peaks behind.

posts.tell: BIGGEST snowpack Utah has EVER recorded
posts.explanation: The source is real and 2023 was a record, but one year isn’t a trend. Real sources can be cherry-picked too.
posts.fact: From 1955 to 2023, April snowpack fell at 81% of measured sites across the western U.S.

sources.label: Utah Water Conditions Update (2023 water year recap)
sources.check: Checked 2026-10-31 (PDF). "Statewide snow water equivalent (SWE) peaked on April 8 at 30.0", which was 216% of normal. This was a new record for Utah."

sources.label: Climate Change Indicators: Snowpack (archived Jan 19, 2025)
sources.check: Checked 2026-10-31. "From 1955 to 2023, April snowpack declined at 81 percent of the sites measured" and "about an 18 percent decline." The live epa.gov URL returned 404, so this links EPA's official archive.

whyNot.legit: Checking the source was smart, but a real fact can still mislead. Check what the post concludes from it.
whyNot.logical-fallacies: The leap is real, but it’s built on one hand-picked year. That specific move is Cherry Picking.

posts.text: app said 8 inches at sundance saturday. we got a dusting 🙄 until they can nail one weekend forecast i’m not trusting climate models about 2100
posts.tell: until they can nail one weekend forecast
posts.explanation: Demanding a perfect weekend forecast before trusting climate projections is an impossible expectation. Weather is one coin flip; climate, a thousand.
posts.fact: NASA: 14 of 17 climate models from 1970–2007 matched later warming once actual CO₂ and other drivers were accounted for.

sources.label: Study Confirms Climate Models are Getting Future Warming Projections Right
sources.check: Checked 2026-10-31. "17 increasingly sophisticated model projections ... developed between 1970 and 2007"; 10 matched closely, and after accounting for actual CO2 and other drivers "the number increased to 14."

sources.label: Evaluating the performance of past climate model projections (Hausfather, Drake, Abbott & Schmidt)
sources.check: Checked 2026-10-31 (NASA GISS abstract page). Models published 1970-2007, "most models examined showing warming consistent with observations."

alsoFair.note: Comparing a weekend forecast to a climate projection is a false analogy. But the main move is the demand: perfect forecasts first, or no trust.

whyNot.cherry-picking: It does lean on one bad forecast, but the move is the demand: perfect forecasts first, or no trust.

posts.text: red air day again 😷 mountains trap it but the pollution is ours. utah DEQ says vehicles make almost half the emissions behind winter smog. carpool if u can 🚗

image.alt: Downtown Salt Lake City towers fading into brown haze, with the mountains barely visible behind them.

posts.explanation: Legit: a checkable source, a claim that matches it, and no overstatement.
posts.fact: Utah DEQ: vehicles make almost half the emissions that form PM2.5 during winter inversions.

sources.label: PM2.5 Moderate Area State Implementation Plans (2009-2014)
sources.check: Checked 2026-10-31. "Vehicles contribute almost half of the emissions that lead to the formation of PM2.5 during winter inversions."

sources.label: Inversions
sources.check: Checked 2026-10-31. "Cold air at the surface gets trapped under a layer of warmer air"; "Pollutants from vehicles, wood burning, area sources, and industry become trapped near the ground."

sources.label: Utah's Air Quality Challenges
sources.check: Checked 2026-10-31. Mobile sources 48%, area sources 39%, point sources 13% "of a typical inversion." (Mobile includes trains and aircraft, not just cars.)

whyNot.fake-experts: Utah DEQ measures Utah’s air for a living. That’s the right expert, not a fake one.
whyNot.logical-fallacies: The logic holds: the mountains trap the air, and the pollution in it is ours.

posts.text: hiked the Bonneville Shoreline Trail today. this whole valley used to be underwater! lake shrank all on its own, no SUVs back then 😉 climate ALWAYS changes

image.alt: A dirt trail along a dry foothill bench high above the Salt Lake Valley.

posts.explanation: True start, false finish. Nature changed past climates, but that doesn’t mean nature is behind today’s change. Wildfires don’t make arson impossible.
posts.fact: NASA: human activities are driving the global warming trend observed since the mid-20th century.

sources.label: The Causes of Climate Change
sources.check: Checked 2026-10-31. "Human activities are driving the global warming trend observed since the mid-20th century."

sources.label: Commonly Asked Questions About Utah's Great Salt Lake & Lake Bonneville
sources.check: Confirm on the page: Lake Bonneville existed ~30,000 to 13,000 years ago, was ~20,000 sq mi at its peak (~18,000 years ago), and shrank as the climate warmed and dried (plus the Bonneville Flood). The page loaded, but its Bonneville section only came back as a summary, not exact text.

sources.label: IPCC AR6 Working Group I, Summary for Policymakers, statement A.1
sources.check: Confirm A.1 reads: "It is unequivocal that human influence has warmed the atmosphere, ocean and land." ipcc.ch blocked the automated check (HTTP 403).

reply.prompt: Which reply would help Uncle Gary most?

options.text: True, it shrank on its own! But that was then. Today’s warming tracks what we burn.
options.feedback: Agrees with the true part, then shows why “natural then” isn’t “natural now.”

options.text: Love that trail! Crazy to picture it underwater. Climate really has always changed, huh? 🏞️
options.feedback: Friendly, but it agrees with the false finish. The myth wins.

options.text: Bonneville changed over thousands of years. NASA says warming since the mid-1900s is human-driven.
options.feedback: True and sourced, but it never says why his reasoning fails.

options.text: Respectfully, Uncle Gary, that’s a classic denier talking point. Maybe read up on it 🙂
options.feedback: Polite, but “denier” and “read up” call him dumb. He’ll dig in.

whyNot.cherry-picking: It isn’t one hand-picked data point. It’s a leap from “natural then” to “natural now.”
whyNot.legit: The trail and the ancient lake are real. That today’s change is natural doesn’t follow.

posts.text: notice how the smoke “crisis” always shows up right when they want new climate rules? 🤔 coincidence?? follow the money. #WakeUpUtah

image.alt: Downtown Salt Lake City seen down a residential street under a gray, smoky sky.

posts.explanation: Conspiracy framing imagines a secret plot and treats any counter-evidence as part of the cover-up. Ask: who exactly is "they"?
posts.fact: A peer-reviewed study found human-caused climate change nearly doubled western U.S. forest fire area from 1984 to 2015.

sources.label: Impact of anthropogenic climate change on wildfire across western US forests (Abatzoglou & Williams), PNAS 113(42)
sources.publisher: FRAMES record of the PNAS abstract
sources.check: Checked 2026-10-31. Abstract: "an additional 4.2 million ha of forest fire area during 1984-2015, nearly doubling the forest fire area expected in its absence." (pnas.org itself blocked the automated check.)

sources.label: Study: Human-caused climate change has doubled western US forest fire area
sources.check: Checked 2026-10-31. "an additional 16,000 square miles of western forest lands to burn between 1984 and 2015."

whyNot.logical-fallacies: The reasoning is bad, but the specific move is a secret plot: “they” and “follow the money.”

posts.text: Remember when the “experts” said the lake would be GONE?? Went out to the state park today and it’s way up. Crisis over!! 🙌

image.alt: Blue water lapping a sandy point at Great Salt Lake State Park, with Antelope Island across the lake.

posts.explanation: One snowy year raised the lake, but it never got healthy and dropped again. Judging by the best year is cherry picking.
posts.fact: The lake peaked in 2023 about 5½ feet above its record low. By January 2026, it was just 3 feet above.

sources.label: How much did Utah's record snowpack help the Great Salt Lake? (Carter Williams, Great Salt Lake Collaborative)
sources.check: Checked 2026-11-04. The lake "topped out at about 4,194.1 feet elevation in mid-June"; "It gained about 5½ feet above the all-time record low"; levels were "about 4 feet below the low-end estimate of what the lake needs to be considered healthy." (Earlier linked to the Standard-Examiner's reprint of this KSL story.)

sources.label: The Great Salt Lake begins the new year teetering near record lows (Leia Larsen)
sources.publisher: The Salt Lake Tribune, via Utah Public Radio
sources.check: Checked 2026-10-31. South end "sits at 4,191.6 feet"; "only three feet higher than its record low" (4,188.5 ft, Nov 2022); the 2023 snowpack gave "a temporary boost." A Salt Lake Tribune story republished by UPR through the Great Salt Lake Collaborative (byline checked 2026-11-04).

sources.label: Emergency Measures Needed to Rescue Great Salt Lake From Ongoing Collapse (Abbott et al.)
sources.check: Checked 2026-10-31. Published Jan 4, 2023; lead author Benjamin W. Abbott. The warning was conditional: "Without a dramatic increase in water flow to the lake in 2023 and 2024."

reply.prompt: Which reply would help Aunt Deb most?

options.text: So fun you went! That snowy year helped, but it’s been dropping again since 💙
options.feedback: Warm, and gently shows why one good year misleads.
options.reaction: Oh! I didn’t know it dropped again 💕

options.text: Actually, by January 2026 it was just 3 feet above its record low. The rise didn’t last.
options.feedback: Accurate, but “Actually” plus numbers feels like a lecture.

options.text: Glad you got out there! Still a ways to go, I hear, but yay for water 💙
options.feedback: Kind, but it never says the rise didn’t last. The myth survives.

options.text: The scientists who study it would probably disagree, Deb. Maybe check the data first? 🙂
options.feedback: Sounds polite, but it implies Deb can’t think. She’ll defend the post.

whyNot.legit: Seeing it yourself is real. Calling the crisis over from one good year is the trick.
whyNot.logical-fallacies: The leap is real, but it rests on one hand-picked year. That specific move is Cherry Picking.

posts.text: NASA’s satellite photos show it: the great salt lake is dying ONLY because of climate change. our water use has nothing to do with it 💔 share if you care

image.alt: Satellite image of the Great Salt Lake in June 2022, ringed by wide pale areas of exposed lakebed.

posts.explanation: Misinformation comes from every side. NASA’s photo shows the shrinking, not the cause; the biggest factor so far is upstream water use.
posts.fact: NASA’s caption for this photo names water diversions and a warmer, drier climate. Diversions have lowered the lake 7 to 11 feet.

sources.label: Rapidly Shrinking Great Salt Lake (MODIS image of the day, June 16, 2022; archived copy)
sources.check: Checked 2026-11-11 (Internet Archive copy; modis.gsfc.nasa.gov refused connections). "Increasing diversion of the water of three rivers feeding the lake for human use and agricultural purposes means less inflow to the lake. Increasingly warm climate and a long-standing drought mean more water evaporating from the lake."

sources.label: Commonly Asked Questions About Utah's Great Salt Lake & Lake Bonneville
sources.check: Checked 2026-10-31 (exact text). "Water resource experts estimate that water appropriations have lowered the lake some 7 to 11 feet, and have roughly halved its volume."

sources.label: Decline of the world's saline lakes (Wurtsbaugh et al.)
sources.check: Confirm the abstract concludes that consumptive water use, not long-term climate change, has greatly reduced Great Salt Lake. nature.com redirected the automated check to a login page.

whyNot.legit: Checking for a source was smart, but this one is stretched: no photo can show “ONLY” one cause.
whyNot.cherry-picking: It doesn’t hand-pick data. It pins everything on one cause, which is broken logic.

posts.text: lol everyone posting about climate change from their iphone in their car 🤡 live in a cave or stop talking
posts.tell: live in a cave or stop talking
posts.explanation: It attacks the messenger and offers a false choice: be perfect or be quiet. PWS 180 calls this “the greatest false choice.”
posts.fact: IPCC: changes in how we use energy and goods could cut end-use emissions 40–70% by 2050, with policy support.

sources.label: IPCC AR6 Working Group III, Summary for Policymakers, statement C.10
sources.check: Confirm C.10: demand-side measures could reduce end-use sector emissions 40-70% by 2050 vs. baseline, and that infrastructure and policy enable those changes. ipcc.ch blocked the automated check (HTTP 403).

sources.label: PWS 180 syllabus, Section 4: "The greatest false choice: personal action and systemic change"
sources.check: Checked 2026-10-31 against the 2026 syllabus (Overview of Schedule, Section 4).

reply.prompt: Which reply would help Brody most?

options.text: Guilty, I drive too! But nobody has to be perfect to want better buses.
options.feedback: Owns the true part, then drops the perfect-or-quiet setup without a fight.
options.reaction: Lol fair. Buses would be nice.

options.text: Haha you’re not wrong 😂 we’re all hypocrites, honestly. No judgment here, man. Do you.
options.feedback: Friendly, but it accepts the false choice, so speaking up still looks fake.

options.text: That’s a false dilemma. Personal choices and systemic change aren’t either/or; we need both.
options.feedback: Correct, but jargon like “false dilemma” sounds like a lecture.
options.reaction: Cool, thanks for the TED talk.

options.text: Says the guy posting from his own iPhone 🙄 maybe practice what you preach.
options.feedback: Fires the same attack back. Now it’s a fight, not a conversation.

whyNot.impossible-expectations: It does demand perfection, but from people, not certainty from the science. That’s a false choice: be perfect or be quiet.
whyNot.fake-experts: No expert is involved. It attacks the people talking instead of what they say.

posts.text: saw this from the Utah Division of Water Resources and it kind of blew my mind 🤯 winter snow is literally our summer water

graphic.caption: of Utah’s water supply comes from snowpack

posts.explanation: Legit: specific, sourced, and it doesn’t stretch the evidence into a bigger claim.
posts.fact: Utah Division of Water Resources: "In Utah, about 95% of our water supply comes from snowpack."

sources.label: Utah Water Conditions Update May 2024
sources.check: Checked 2026-10-31. "In Utah, about 95% of our water supply comes from snowpack."

whyNot.cherry-picking: It’s one number, but it’s the statewide share, not a hand-picked moment.

posts.text: the SUN controls the climate. always has. more sunspots = warmer earth. the rest is politics ☀️ #DoYourOwnResearch
posts.explanation: The sun matters, but this squeezes a complex system into one cause and ignores what the sun has done lately.
posts.fact: NASA: solar energy reaching Earth shows no net increase since the 1950s, while global temperature has risen markedly.

sources.label: Is the Sun causing global warming?
sources.check: Checked 2026-10-31. Solar energy shows "no net increase since the 1950s. Over the same period, global temperature has risen markedly."

whyNot.cherry-picking: It does skip what the sun has done lately, but the core move is one cause for everything.

posts.text: the “consensus” is falling apart 👇 1,600 scientists can’t all be wrong

graphic.headline: 1,600 Scientists Sign Declaration: “There Is No Climate Emergency”

posts.explanation: Signatures aren’t evidence, so check who signed. Over 99% of published climate research agrees humans are warming Earth.
posts.fact: The real 2023 declaration’s signers included engineers, doctors, lawyers and economists. An earlier version had only 10 self-described climate scientists among 1,200 names.

sources.label: Did 1,609 scientists sign a declaration saying ‘there is no climate emergency’? Not quite
sources.check: Checked 2026-11-04. The 1,609-name list "included engineers, doctors, lawyers, mathematicians, architects, entrepreneurs, and economists"; "Those with climate expertise were few." Of the earlier 1,200-name version, "Only 10 of the signatories described themselves as climatologists or climate scientists, Agence France-Presse found."

sources.label: Greater than 99% consensus on human caused climate change in the peer-reviewed scientific literature (Lynas, Houlton & Perry)
sources.check: Checked 2026-10-31. Abstract: consensus "exceeds 99% in the peer reviewed scientific literature."

whyNot.logical-fallacies: “1,600 can’t be wrong” is a numbers fallacy, but the pitch is the signers as experts. Few study climate.
whyNot.conspiracy: It doesn’t claim a secret plot. It leans on a crowd of names as experts.

posts.text: scientists can’t even say exactly WHEN the lake bottoms out. until they can, why should farmers give up water? 🤷‍♂️
posts.tell: can’t even say exactly WHEN the lake bottoms out
posts.explanation: Demanding an exact date before acting is an impossible expectation. Unsure timing doesn’t change which way the lake is heading.
posts.fact: In 2023, researchers warned the lake faced collapse without much more inflow. In January 2026 it sat near record lows.

sources.label: Emergency Measures Needed to Rescue Great Salt Lake From Ongoing Collapse (Abbott et al.)
sources.check: Checked 2026-10-31. Published Jan 4, 2023; lead author Benjamin W. Abbott. The warning was conditional: "Without a dramatic increase in water flow to the lake in 2023 and 2024."

sources.label: The Great Salt Lake begins the new year teetering near record lows (Leia Larsen)
sources.publisher: The Salt Lake Tribune, via Utah Public Radio
sources.check: Checked 2026-10-31. South end "sits at 4,191.6 feet"; "only three feet higher than its record low" (4,188.5 ft, Nov 2022); the 2023 snowpack gave "a temporary boost." A Salt Lake Tribune story republished by UPR through the Great Salt Lake Collaborative (byline checked 2026-11-04).

whyNot.logical-fallacies: Every trick is bad reasoning. When a post demands an exact date before anyone acts, the specific name is Impossible Expectations.
whyNot.cherry-picking: Nothing is hand-picked here. It refuses to act until the timing is certain.

posts.text: they literally change the old temperature records to make the past look colder 🤔 ask yourself WHY

graphic.headline: NOAA Caught Rewriting Utah’s Temperature History

posts.explanation: Conspiracy framing turns routine, published corrections into a secret plot. The methods are in peer-reviewed papers anyone can read.
posts.fact: Scientists correct records for station moves and new instruments. Worldwide, adjustments actually reduce the long-term warming trend.

sources.label: The U.S. Historical Climatology Network monthly temperature data, version 2 (Menne, Williams & Vose)
sources.publisher: Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society
sources.check: Checked 2026-11-01 (PDF). Records are "corrected" for "historical changes in station location, instrumentation, and observing practice."

sources.label: Explainer: How data adjustments affect global temperature records (Zeke Hausfather)
sources.check: Checked 2026-11-01. "adjustments actually have the net effect of reducing the amount of long-term warming" (mostly from ocean data; land adjustments add warming).

whyNot.legit: A headline isn’t evidence. NOAA publishes how and why it adjusts old records.
whyNot.logical-fallacies: The reasoning is bad, but the specific move is a cover-up: “ask yourself WHY.”

posts.text: they’re spraying chemicals over our mountains and calling it “cloud seeding” ✈️💨 that’s why everyone’s sick this winter. WAKE UP
posts.explanation: This turns a public program into a cover story and pins unrelated problems on it. What evidence links the two?
posts.fact: Utah’s cloud seeding is a public, state-backed program using a 2% silver iodide solution to boost snowpack since the mid-1970s.

sources.label: Annual Cloud Seeding Report, Northern Utah Program, 2022-2023 Winter Season
sources.publisher: North American Weather Consultants, for the Utah Division of Water Resources and partners
sources.check: Checked 2026-11-01 (PDF). Generators use "a 2% silver iodide solution"; goal is "to augment wintertime snowpack"; "operational programs in Utah since the mid-1970s"; cost sharing from the Utah Division of Water Resources.

whyNot.logical-fallacies: It does jump to conclusions, but through a cover story: “calling it cloud seeding.”

posts.text: -15 in Logan this morning. global warming my foot 🥶😂
posts.explanation: One frigid morning in one valley says nothing about the planet’s long-term average. That’s cherry picking with a thermometer.
posts.fact: Cold snaps still happen, just less often. In the 2000s, the West set over two record highs for every record low.

sources.label: Record high temperatures far outpace record lows across U.S. (on Meehl et al. 2009, Geophysical Research Letters)
sources.check: Checked 2026-11-04. "daily record high temperatures occurred twice as often as record lows over the last decade"; warming "was more pronounced in the western United States, where the ratio was more than two to one."

reply.prompt: Which reply would help Grandpa most?

options.text: Stay warm, Grandpa! Cold mornings still happen. They’re just getting rarer while record-hot days pile up.
options.feedback: Kind, then trades one cold morning for the bigger pattern.
options.reaction: Huh. Rarer, huh? I’ll take it 🥶

options.text: Brr, stay warm, Grandpa! 🥶 Weather’s been so crazy lately. Who even knows anymore?
options.feedback: Kind, but it agrees nobody knows. He leaves more sure he’s right.

options.text: People say a cold day disproves warming, but the West sets over two heat records per cold one.
options.feedback: Accurate, but it repeats the myth first and reads like a lecture.

options.text: Grandpa 😂 love you, but that’s literally the oldest myth in the book. Weather isn’t climate!
options.feedback: Affectionate, but it laughs at him. People defend ideas that get mocked.

whyNot.logical-fallacies: The leap is real, but it rests on one cold morning. That specific move is Cherry Picking.
whyNot.impossible-expectations: Grandpa isn’t demanding certainty. He’s treating one morning as the whole trend.

posts.text: U of U researchers found dust from the dried lakebed carries arsenic and other metals. one more reason to refill the lake 💧

graphic.headline: Just how dangerous is Great Salt Lake dust? New research looks for clues

posts.explanation: Legit: it names who found it and doesn’t overstate it: metals in the dust, not mass poisoning.
posts.fact: Researchers found lakebed dust with arsenic above EPA residential soil screening levels. How much reaches neighborhoods is still being studied.

sources.label: Just how dangerous is Great Salt Lake dust? New research looks for clues
sources.check: Checked 2026-11-01. Lakebed dust had "levels of arsenic and lithium that exceed the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency's soil residential" screening levels (Atmospheric Environment, 2024; lab-aerosolized sediment samples).

sources.label: Projecting Impacts of Great Salt Lake Dust Exposure
sources.check: Checked 2026-11-01. A modeling study of how dust from the dry lakebed reaches the Wasatch Front; "Aeolian dust from the shrinking Great Salt Lake (GSL) is a major concern."

whyNot.fake-experts: These are scientists studying their own field. That’s the right kind of expert.
whyNot.logical-fallacies: It doesn’t overstate: metals in the dust, not mass poisoning. Wanting the lake refilled follows from that.

posts.text: AQI 162 from the fires 🔥 at this level even healthy people can start to feel it. skipping my run today
posts.tell: even healthy people can start to feel it
posts.explanation: No source named, but it matches the official AQI scale without overstating. Check the claim, not the citation.
posts.fact: AirNow: at 151–200 (“Unhealthy”), some members of the general public may feel health effects; sensitive groups may feel worse.

sources.label: AQI Basics
sources.check: Checked 2026-11-01. Unhealthy (151 to 200): "Some members of the general public may experience health effects; members of sensitive groups may experience more serious health effects."

whyNot.logical-fallacies: Nothing breaks here: AQI 162 really is “Unhealthy,” and skipping a run is a reasonable response.
whyNot.cherry-picking: It’s one reading, but it’s about today’s air and today’s run. It isn’t claiming a trend.

posts.text: china emits WAY more than utah. nothing we do here matters so stop telling me to carpool 🙄
posts.explanation: A bigger polluter elsewhere doesn’t excuse ours. Every state is a small slice of global CO₂, and our exhaust fills our valleys.
posts.fact: Burning fuel here adds CO₂ and makes our smog, so cutting it helps both. Vehicles make almost half our winter smog emissions.

sources.label: The Utah Roadmap: Positive Solutions on Climate and Air Quality
sources.publisher: Kem C. Gardner Policy Institute, University of Utah
sources.check: Checked 2026-11-04. (PDF, p. 2, "The Air Quality/Changing Climate Connection") "Reducing air emissions throughout Utah benefits both air quality and changing climate issues."

sources.label: PM2.5 Moderate Area State Implementation Plans (2009-2014)
sources.check: Checked 2026-10-31. "Vehicles contribute almost half of the emissions that lead to the formation of PM2.5 during winter inversions."

sources.label: Utah's Air Quality Challenges
sources.check: Checked 2026-10-31. Mobile sources 48%, area sources 39%, point sources 13% "of a typical inversion." (Mobile includes trains and aircraft, not just cars.)

reply.prompt: Which reply would help Kade most?

options.text: True, China’s bigger. But our smog is homemade, and driving less helps lungs and climate.
options.feedback: Grants the true part, then shows why local action still pays off.
options.reaction: Huh. Never thought about the smog.

options.text: Haha fair, it does feel kind of pointless sometimes 😅 no pressure, man.
options.feedback: Friendly, but agreeing nothing matters is the fallacy itself.

reply.prompt: Which reply would help Tyler most?

options.text: You’d know the plant! But that brown layer isn’t water. It’s pollution trapped by cold air.
options.feedback: Gives him credit, then swaps “fog” for what’s really in the air.

options.text: People think inversions are just fog, but that’s a myth. It’s pollution trapped under warm air.
options.feedback: Correct, but calling his view a myth feels like a gotcha.
options.reaction: Not a myth. I see it daily.

options.text: Ha, you’d know better than me! It gets so thick some days. Stay safe out there 🙌
options.feedback: Friendly, but it hands him the point. “Just fog” now has your vote.

options.text: No offense, Tyler, but working at a refinery doesn’t exactly make you an air quality expert 😅
options.feedback: Right issue, but the dig makes it personal. He’ll defend himself.

whyNot.logical-fallacies: The logic is weak, but it leans on insider credentials: “I work at the refinery, trust me.”
whyNot.legit: Working near a smokestack isn’t measuring the air. DEQ’s measurements say otherwise.
